newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Arab dies in crash, PLO says was shot.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Arab dies in crash, PLO says was shot.

text.p: A man travelling in a car from the West Bank towards Jerusalem was killed early on Wednesday at an Israeli roadblock in what Palestinians said was a deliberate shooting and Israelis called a crash.

Israeli police said the driver refused their order to stop at a roadblock. They said they shot at the car's tyres and it slammed into a truck. A police spokeswoman said the identity of neither the driver nor the dead man was immediately known.
Jibril Rujoub, head of Palestinian Preventive Security in the West Bank, said the man was shot by Israeli undercover units. The Israeli army denied it.
Another senior PLO security official said the killing did not take place at a roadblock, but on a main road in Arab East Jerusalem.

Television pictures taken by Israel's Channel Two showed the front left tyre was punctured, the front right side of the hood was bent, there was a gunshot hole in the back right window and there was no blood inside the car.

The pictures, taken after the body was apparently removed, showed the car by the side of the highway, its headlights on and intact and four Israeli police vans stationed around it. A remote-controlled bomb detonator went from one of the police vans towards the car and then back.
Police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin said Israeli border police at Hizmeh roadblock north of Jerusalem signalled the car to stop but the driver ignored them.

"The border police said they shot in the air and then the car tried to overrun them. They said they shot in the air again and at the tyres but the car didn't stop and collided with a truck," Menuhin said.
"The passenger in the car was injured and taken to hospital where he died. His identity is unknown. The driver ran away."

But the senior PLO security official said the "Israelis were lying about the way they killed the Palestinian man because he was shot dead on a main road inside Jerusalem and very far from Hizmeh roadblock."
"The Palestinian was killed by undercover units in civilian clothes and not by the army," said the PLO official who did not want to be identified.
